newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Nigerian minister says 15 months to democracy.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian minister says 15 months to democracy.

text.p: A Nigerian government minister said on Tuesday that his country, Africa's largest oil producer, was about 15 months away from democracy and an end to military rule.
Commerce and Tourism Minister Jubrila Ayinla told a sub-Saharan oils and minerals conference that the country was on a "one-way street to democracy".
"We have a military government in place but we are on a one-way street to democracy. We realise that the military has no role in government," Ayinla said.
He said the government had committed itself to moving to democracy, but the transition was hampered by the huge population of more than 100 million and 250 ethnic groups.
Ayinla said the government hoped to have established a democracy in 15 months.
"Fifteen months is a very short time in the life of a nation. We think that in 15 months we will be able to have in place a democratic government in Nigeria," Ayinla said.
He said Nigeria would continue to act on crises in other African countries as it did in Sierra Leone.
"We believe that there is no crisis in any part of Africa that doesn't affect Nigeria."
Ayinla called for greater cooperation between African countries on trade and said the continent should move towards forming a trade bloc.
